move: The snail will move slowly across the leaf.
Can you move your chair closer to the table?
Stay still and do not move at all.
prove: A photo can prove that we went to the beach.
Can you prove that the box is empty?
Look at the map to prove you are right.
improve: Reading every night helps me improve at spelling.
Daily practice will improve your football.
Painting more will improve my pictures!
sure: Are you sure this is the right bus?
Dad felt sure the shop was open on Sunday.
Check twice to be sure the door is shut.
sugar: Stir the sugar into your hot tea.
Do the biscuits have sugar on top?
The sweet white sugar melted in the cup.
water: Turn the tap and water will pour out.
Pour some water on the thirsty plant.
The fish swim in clean water.
money: How much money is in the piggy bank?
We need money to buy bread at the shop.
Gran gave me money for my birthday.
want: Do you want jam or honey on toast?
I want to play on the swings!
The puppy will want a walk after tea.
squash: I squash the clay flat with my hand.
Hold the grapes gently so you do not squash them.
Jump on the empty box to squash it flat!
brother: Is that boy your brother or your cousin?
My little brother is learning to walk.
I share my bedroom with my big brother.

rejected.s: Use a ruler to prove the table is long.
rejected.reason: checker: Proving a table is 'long' with a ruler is odd logic and may confuse a child.

rejected.s: How can we improve our garden this spring?
rejected.reason: checker: 'How can we water our garden this spring?' also makes sense. (also fits: water)

rejected.s: Are you sure it is Tuesday today?
rejected.reason: machine rule 6: too like another candidate

rejected.s: Ants like the sugar spilled on the floor!
rejected.reason: machine rule 4: not on the word lists: spilled

rejected.s: Too much sugar is bad for your teeth.
rejected.reason: checker: It moralises about food and health, which is too close to diet talk.

rejected.s: We need flour, eggs and sugar to bake.
rejected.reason: checker: 'Flour, eggs and water' could also make sense for some baking. (also fits: water)

rejected.s: Would you want to come to my party?
rejected.reason: checker: 'Would you want to come' is less natural than 'would you like to come'.

rejected.s: Press down hard to squash the empty can.
rejected.reason: machine rule 5: word overlap with the meaning is 67%

rejected.s: Please do not squash my ripe plums!
rejected.reason: checker: 'Please do not move my ripe plums!' also makes sense. (also fits: move)

rejected.s: Big books will squash the bread at the bottom.
rejected.reason: checker: Without saying 'in the bag', the scene is unclear for a child.
